'''Threema''' is a [[Commercial software|paid]] [[Cross-platform software|cross-platform]] [[Encryption|encrypted]] [[instant messaging]] app developed by Threema AG in Switzerland and launched in 2012. Users can make voice and [[Videotelephony|video calls]], send photos, files, and voice notes, share locations, and join [[Group chat|groups]]. The service offers [[end-to-end encryption]]. Unlike many other popular secure messaging apps, Threema does not require [[Telephone number|phone numbers]] or [[email address|email addresses]] for registration, only a one-time purchase that can be paid via an [[app store]] or anonymously with [[Bitcoin]] or [[cash]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Support – Threema |url=https://threema.ch/en/support |access-date=2024-02-10 |website=threema.ch |language=en}}</ref>

Threema is available on [[Android (operating system)|Android]] and [[iOS]], and has clients for [[HarmonyOS]], [[Linux]], [[macOS]] and [[Microsoft Windows|Windows]]. It can be accessed via [[web browser]] but requires a mobile app to function.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Happich |first1=Julien |title=Privacy gains traction with secure messaging apps |date=September 23, 2014 |url=http://www.electronics-eetimes.com/en/privacy-gains-traction-with-secure-messaging-apps.html?cmp_id=7&news_id=222922448&vID=13&page=1 |website=Electronic Engineering Times Europe |access-date=December 21, 2015 |archive-date=September 23, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923235418/http://www.electronics-eetimes.com/en/privacy-gains-traction-with-secure-messaging-apps.html?cmp_id=7&news_id=222922448&vID=13&page=1 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Features ==

The service claims to be based on the [[privacy by design]] principles by not requiring a phone number or other [[Personal data|personally identifiable information]]. This helps anonymize the users to a degree.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://threema.ch/press-files/cryptography_whitepaper.pdf|title=Cryptography Whitepaper|access-date=October 30, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://threema.ch/en/faq/privacy_protection|title=FAQ – Privacy Protection|access-date=October 30, 2020}}</ref>

Threema uses a randomly generated user ID, created after the initial app launch, instead of requiring a linked email address or phone number to send messages. It is possible to find other users by phone number or email address, if the user allows the app to synchronize their address book.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://threema.ch/en/faq/addressbook_data  |title=Will my address book data be sent to your servers? |website=threema.ch |access-date=December 2, 2014}}{{third-party-inline|date=December 2014}}</ref> 

Linking a phone number or email address to a Threema ID is optional. Hence, the service can be used anonymously. 

Users can verify the identity of their Threema contacts by scanning their [[QR code]] when they meet in person. The QR code contains the [[Public-key cryptography|public key]] of the user, which is cryptographically tied to the ID and will not change during the lifetime of the identity. 

Using this strong authentication feature, users can make sure they have the correct public key from their chat partners, which provides additional security against a [[man-in-the-middle attack]]. 

Threema classifies contacts according to three verification trust levels. The verification level of each contact is displayed in the Threema application as dots next to the corresponding contact.

In addition to text messaging, users can make voice and video calls, share locations, voice messages, and send media or other files.<ref name="What features does Threema offer">{{cite web |url=https://threema.ch/en/faq/features |title=What features does Threema offer? |website=threema.ch}}</ref> A [[Web application|web app]], Threema Web, can be used on desktop devices, but only as long as the phone with the Threema installation of the user is online. There is a beta for iOS users, which allows for the phone to be offline while using a desktop app.

In addition to one-to-one chats, Threema offers group chats with up to 256 people. Files are limited to 50MB per file.<ref name="What features does Threema offer"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://threema.ch/en/faq/file_message |title=How can I send a file? |website=threema.ch}}</ref> It is also possible to create polls in personal or group chats.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Threema integriert Umfrage-Funktion |trans-title=Threema integrates survey function |first=Stefan |last=Bordel |date=January 12, 2015 |url=http://www.com-magazin.de/news/smartphone/threema-integriert-umfrage-funktion-871882.html |website=com! – Das Computer-Magazin |access-date=October 12, 2015 |language=de}}</ref>

To emulate the 'Saved Messages' feature available in other messengers, one can create a group with only oneself as a member. For licensing and privacy reasons, Threema does not include a GIF library natively, but it is compatible with GIF keyboards and plays animations seamlessly in the chat.

== Software ==

Threema is developed by the Swiss company Threema AG.<ref name="zefix">{{cite web |url=https://zefix.ch/de/search/entity/list/firm/1440681 |url-status=dead |title=Swiss company registry entry for Threema AG |author=Swiss Confederation |website=zefix.ch |access-date=September 8, 2026 }}</ref> The [[Server (computing)|servers]] are in [[Switzerland]] and the development is based in [[Pfäffikon, Schwyz|Pfäffikon SZ]]. As of May 2021, Threema had 10 million users<ref>{{Cite web|last=Jungfer|first=Martin|date=28 May 2021|title=Number of Threema users climbed to over 10 million|url=https://www.digitec.ch/en/page/number-of-threema-users-climbed-to-over-10-million-20061|access-date=10 Aug 2021|website=digitec.ch|archive-date=August 10, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210810194254/https://www.digitec.ch/en/page/number-of-threema-users-climbed-to-over-10-million-20061|url-status=dead}}</ref> and the business version, Threema Work, was used by 2 million users across 5,000 companies and organizations.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Threema's Success Story: From the Company's Founding to Today|url=https://threema.ch/press-files/1_press_info/press_threema_story_en.pdf|access-date=May 11, 2021}}</ref>

At the end of July, 2021 Threema introduced the ability for companies to host the messenger on their own server, primarily intended for companies with significantly high privacy concerns.<ref>{{Cite web|date=27 Jul 2021|title=Messenger for companies and authorities: Threema offers an on-premise version|url=https://marketresearchtelecast.com/messenger-for-companies-and-authorities-threema-offers-an-on-premise-version-2/113628/|access-date=10 Aug 2021|website=Market Research Telecast}}{{Dead link|date=September 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

=== Clients ===
With Threema Web, a client for [[web browser]]s, Threema can be used from other devices like [[desktop computer]]s, though only as long as the original device is online.

Threema optionally supports [[Android Wear]] [[smartwatches|smartwatch]] and [[Android Auto]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://threema.ch/en/blog/posts/big-update-for-android-and-ios-20 |title=Big Update for Android |website=threema.ch |date=December 9, 2014 }}</ref> Threema launched support for end-to-end encrypted video calls on August 10, 2020. The calls are person-to-person with group calls unavailable.<ref name="Cimpanu"/>

The application does not allow the self-deletion of messages after a period defined by the interlocutors.
The application does prevent screenshots in conversations when configured to do so.

=== Architecture ===

The entire communication via Threema is [[End-to-end encryption|end-to-end encrypted]]. During the initial setup, the application generates a [[key pair]] and sends the [[public key]] to the server while keeping the private key on the user's device.<ref name="crypto_authorities">{{cite web |url=https://threema.ch/en/faq.html#crypto_authorities |title=Could you decrypt my messages? |website=threema.ch |access-date=July 5, 2014}}{{third-party-inline|date=December 2014}}</ref> The application then encrypts all messages and files that are sent to other Threema users with their respective public keys.<ref name=":1" /><ref name="net-security.org">{{Cite web |title=Secure mobile messaging with Threema |url=http://www.net-security.org/review.php?id=333 |first=Mirko |last=Zorz |date= September 17, 2014 |website=Help Net Security}}</ref> Once a message is delivered successfully, it is immediately deleted from the [[Server (computing)|servers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://threema.ch/en/faq/message_storage |title=How long do messages stay in queue for delivery? |website=threema.ch |access-date=September 20, 2017}}</ref>

The encryption process used by Threema is based on the [[open-source software|open-source]] library [[NaCl (software)|NaCl]]. Threema uses asymmetric [[Elliptic curve cryptography|ECC]]-based encryption, with 256-bit strength. Threema offers a "Validation Logging" feature that makes it possible to confirm that messages are end-to-end encrypted using the [[NaCl (software)|NaCl]] Networking and Cryptography library.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://threema.ch/validation/ |title=Threema Validation |website=threema.ch |access-date=September 20, 2017 |archive-date=November 25, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181125211914/https://threema.ch/validation/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> 

In August 2015, Threema was subjected to an external security audit.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://threema.ch/en/faq/code_audit/ |title=External Audit |website=threema.ch |access-date=September 20, 2017}}</ref> Researchers from cnlab confirmed that Threema allows secure end-to-end encryption, and claimed that they were unable to identify any weaknesses in the implementation. 

Cnlab researchers also confirmed that Threema provides anonymity to its users and handles contacts and other user data as advertised.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://threema.ch/press-files/2_documentation/external_audit_security_statement.pdf |title=Security Review Threema: Security Statement |date=November 2, 2015 |website=threema.ch |access-date=October 30, 2020}}</ref><ref name="audit">{{cite web |last1=Schirrmacher |first1=Dennis |title=Threema-Audit abgeschlossen: "Ende-zu-Ende-Verschlüsselung ohne Schwächen" |trans-title=Threema Audit Completed: "End-to-End Encryption Without Weakness" |url=http://www.heise.de/security/meldung/Threema-Audit-abgeschlossen-Ende-zu-Ende-Verschluesselung-ohne-Schwaechen-2868866.html |date=November 3, 2015 |website=Heise.de |access-date=October 30, 2020 |language=de}}</ref>

==History==
Threema was founded in December 2012 by Manuel Kasper.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nzz.ch/nzzas/nzz-am-sonntag/threema-schweizer-startup-privatshaere-kryptografie-ld.815 |title=Kryptografie-App Threema: Schweizer sorgen für Privatsphäre |trans-title=Cryptography app Threema: Swiss ensure privacy |first=Marco |last=Metzler |date=June 28, 2015 |newspaper=[[Neue Zürcher Zeitung]] |access-date=October 8, 2015 |language=de}}</ref> The company was initially called Kasper Systems GmbH.<ref name="mailify">{{cite web |url=http://www.mailify.de/2014/07/im-interview-threema/ |title=Im Interview: Threema |date=July 23, 2014 |access-date=October 11, 2015 |website=Mailify |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140802204127/http://www.mailify.de/2014/07/im-interview-threema |archive-date=August 2, 2014 |language=de}}</ref> Martin Blatter and Silvan Engeler joined Kasper to develop an Android application that was released in early 2013.<ref name="freitag">{{cite news |title=Der Schlossherr |url=https://www.freitag.de/autoren/der-freitag/der-schlossherr |newspaper=[[Der Freitag]] |access-date=October 11, 2015 |issn=0945-2095 |language=de |first=Hakan |last=Tanriverdi}}</ref>

In Summer 2013, the [[Global surveillance disclosures (2013–present)|Snowden leaks]] helped create an interest in Threema, boosting the user numbers to the hundreds of thousands.<ref name="businessinsider">{{Cite web |last1=Price |first1=Rob |title=Germany's most popular paid app is a secure messenger loved by millions — now it's taking on the US |date=June 18, 2015 |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/threema-encryption-messaging-app-america-launch-isis-2015-6 |website=[[Business Insider]] UK |access-date=October 11, 2015}}</ref> When Facebook took over [[WhatsApp]] in February 2014, Threema got 200,000 new users, doubling its userbase in 24 hours.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bye Bye, WhatsApp: Germans Switch To Threema For Privacy Reasons |url=https://techcrunch.com/2014/02/21/bye-bye-whatsapp-germans-switch-to-threema-for-privacy-reasons/ |first=Romain |last=Dillet |date=February 21, 2014 |website=[[TechCrunch]]}}</ref> Around 80% percent of those new users came from Germany. By March 2014 Threema had 1.2&nbsp;million users.<ref name="freitag" />

In Spring 2014, operations were transferred to the newly created Threema GmbH.<ref name="mailify" /><ref>{{cite web |title=Threema GmbH, Pfäffikon SZ |url=https://www.shabex.ch/co/threema_gmbh_CH-130.4.020.462-0.htm |website=Shabex.ch |access-date=October 11, 2015}}</ref> Martin Blatter took over the position of CEO.<ref name="nzz_blatter">{{cite news |author=Rafaela Roth |url=https://www.nzz.ch/gesellschaft/martin-blatter-mit-gruender-threema-app-arbeitet-fuer-die-armee-ld.1786310 |title=Der Mann, der die Camouflage-App der Schweizer Armee entwickelte |newspaper=[[Neue Zürcher Zeitung]] |date=2022-01-08 |access-date=2025-01-15 |language=de}}</ref>

In December 2014, Apple listed Threema as the most-sold app of 2014 at the German App Store.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.focus.de/digital/handy/iphone/telekommunikation-ios-highlights-die-besten-apps-des-jahres_id_4330110.html |title=iOS-Highlights: Die besten Apps des Jahres |trans-title=The best apps of the year |date=December 9, 2014 |website=[[Focus (German magazine)|Focus]] |language=de |access-date=March 1, 2016}}</ref>

In 2020, Threema expanded with video calls,<ref name="Cimpanu">{{Cite web |title=Threema joins the ranks of E2EE chat apps that support encrypted video calls |last=Cimpanu |first=Catalin|date=August 11, 2020 |url= https://www.zdnet.com/article/threema-joins-the-ranks-of-e2ee-chat-apps-that-support-encrypted-video-calls/ |website=ZDNet |access-date=October 30, 2020 |language=en}}</ref> plans to open-source its client-side apps and introduce reproducible builds of them,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Threema E2EE chat app to go 'fully open source' within months |last=Cimpanu |first=Catalin|date=September 4, 2020 |url= https://www.zdnet.com/article/threema-e2ee-chat-app-to-go-fully-open-source-within-months/ |website=ZDNet |access-date=October 30, 2020 |language=en}}</ref> as well as introduce Threema Education, a variation of Threema intended for education institutions.

In September 2020, Threema was acquired by AFINUM, a German private equity firm based in Munich.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AFINUM acquires Threema |url=https://www.vischer.com/en/knowledge/deals-cases/afinum-acquires-threema-38719/ |access-date=2025-06-21 |website=www.vischer.com |language=en}}</ref>

During the second week of 2021, Threema saw a quadrupling of daily downloads spurred on by [[WhatsApp#Recent (2016–present)|controversial privacy changes]] in the WhatsApp messaging service. A spokesperson for the company also confirmed that Threema had risen to the top of the charts for paid applications in Germany, Switzerland, and Austria.<ref>{{Cite news|last=|first=|date=January 13, 2021|title=WhatsApp-Konkurrenten verzeichnen starken Nutzeranstieg|language=German|work=Die Zeit|url=https://www.zeit.de/digital/datenschutz/2021-01/messengerdienste-whatsapp-konkurrenz-starker-nutzeranstieg-threema-telegram-signal-datenschutz|access-date=January 13, 2021}}</ref> This trend continued into the third week of the year, with the head of Marketing & Sales confirming that downloads had increased to ten times the regular amount, leading to "hundreds of thousands of new users each day".<ref>{{Cite news|last=Pladson|first=Kristie|date=January 18, 2021|title=WhatsApp controversy highlights growing fears about data privacy|work=DW|url=https://www.dw.com/en/whatsapp-controversy-highlights-growing-fears-about-data-privacy/a-56266093|access-date=January 19, 2021}}</ref>

In October 2022, researchers from ETH Zurich reported multiple vulnerabilities affecting Threema's security against network, server and client-based attacks. A new release fixing these issues was released in November 2022 and the vulnerabilities were announced publicly in January 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Three Lessons from Threema: Analysis of a Secure Messenger |url=https://breakingthe3ma.app/ |access-date=2023-01-10 |website=breakingthe3ma.app}}</ref>

In September 2024, CEO Martin Blatter and the remaining founders and original developers left the company and Robin Simon, a former executive from [[TX Group]] became CEO.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Meet Robin Simon at PMF |url=https://productmanagementfestival.com/speaker/robin-simon-f9c97 |access-date=2025-06-25 |website=productmanagementfestival.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="shab">{{cite web|author=Bundesamt für Justiz (BJ) |url=https://www.shab.ch/shabforms/servlet/Search?EID=7&DOCID=1006127945 |title=Mutation Threema GmbH, Freienbach |website=Schweizerisches Handelsamtsblatt |date=2024-09-12 |access-date=2025-08-16 |language=de|format=PDF}}</ref>

On 13 January 2026, the German private equity firm Comitis Capital announced that they reached an agreement with Threema Holding AG to acquire the company.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2026-01-13 |title=Comitis Capital acquires Threema |url=https://www.heise.de/en/news/Comitis-Capital-acquires-Threema-11138748.html |access-date=2026-01-13 |website=[[Heise Group|heise online]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Related products==

=== Threema Work ===
On May 25, 2016, Threema Work, a corporate version of Threema, was released. Threema Work offers extended administration and deployment capabilities.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://work.threema.ch/en|title=The messenger for organizations|website=work.threema.ch}}</ref> Threema Work is based on a yearly subscription model.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://work.threema.ch/en/offer|title=Pricing Threema Work}}</ref>

=== Threema Gateway ===
On March 20, 2015, Threema released a gateway for companies. Similar to an [[SMS gateway]], businesses can use it to send messages to their users who have Threema installed.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Iseli|first=Marc|url=http://www.handelszeitung.ch/unternehmen/us-feldzug-von-threema-geraet-ins-stocken-869170|title=US-Feldzug von Threema gerät ins Stocken|date=September 28, 2015|newspaper=[[Handelszeitung]]|access-date=October 12, 2015|language=de|trans-title=US campaign of Threema is stalled|issn=1422-8971|archive-date=June 20, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240620100350/https://www.handelszeitung.ch/unternehmen/us-feldzug-von-threema-geraet-ins-stocken-869170|url-status=dead}}</ref> The code for the Threema Gateway [[Software development kit|SDK]] is open for developers and available on [[GitHub]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://github.com/threema-ch|title=Threema GmbH|website=GitHub|access-date=September 20, 2017}}</ref>

=== Threema Broadcast ===
On August 9, 2018, Threema released Threema Broadcast, a tool for [[Business communication#Directional business communication|top-down communication]]. Similar to emails in electronic [[newsletter]]s, Threema messages can be sent to any number of feed subscribers, and the Threema Broadcast allows to create [[chatbot]]s.

=== Threema Education ===
On September 10, 2020, Threema released Threema Education, a version of its messenger designed for education institutions. The app integrates Threema Broadcast and requires a one-time payment for each device used. It's intended for use by teachers, students, and parents.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://threema.ch/en/blog/posts/educach-en|title=Threema Education: Framework Contract with educa.ch|date=September 10, 2020|access-date=October 25, 2020}}</ref>

=== Threema OnPrem ===
On July 27, 2021, Threema released Threema OnPrem, a version of the messenger which could be hosted on a company's own servers for maximum security purposes.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Threema OnPrem|url=https://threema.ch/en/onprem|access-date=10 Aug 2021|website=Threema}}</ref>

== Privacy ==
Since Threema's servers are in Switzerland, they are subject to the Swiss federal law on data protection. The data center is [[ISO/IEC 27001]]-certified.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://work.threema.ch/docs/threema_privacy-security_en.pdf |title=Reference Sheet Privacy and Security |website=threema.ch |page=2}}</ref> 

Linking a phone number and/or email address to a Threema ID is optional; when doing so, only [[checksum]] values ([[SHA-256]] [[HMAC]] with a static key) of the email address and/or phone number are sent to the server.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://threema.ch/press-files/cryptography_whitepaper.pdf |title=Threema Cryptography Whitepaper |website=threema.ch |page=11}}</ref> 

Due to the small number of possible digit combinations of a telephone number, the phone number associated with a checksum could be determined by [[Brute-force attack|brute force]]. The transmitted data is [[Transport Layer Security|TLS]]-secured. The address book data is kept only in the [[volatile memory]] of the server and is deleted immediately after synchronizing contacts.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://threema.ch/en/faq/addressbook_data |title=Will my address book data be sent to your servers? |website=threema.ch}}</ref> 

If a user chooses to link a phone number or email address with their Threema ID, they can remove the phone number or email address at any time.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://threema.ch/en/faq/unlink |title=How can I unlink my Threema ID from an email address or phone number? |website=threema.ch}}</ref> Should a user ever lose their device (and their private key), they can revoke their Threema ID if a revocation password for that ID has been set.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://myid.threema.ch/revoke |title=Revoke your ID |website=threema.ch}}</ref>

Groups are solely managed on users’ devices and group messages are sent to each recipient as an individual message, encrypted with the respective public key. Thus, group compositions are not directly exposed to the server.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://threema.ch/press-files/cryptography_whitepaper.pdf |title=Threema Cryptography Whitepaper |website=threema.ch |page=5}}</ref>

Data (including media files) stored on the users’ devices is encrypted with [[Advanced Encryption Standard|AES 256]]. On Android, it can be additionally protected by a [[passphrase]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://threema.ch/en/faq/crypto_local |title=Are messages encrypted when they are stored on my device? |website=threema.ch}}</ref>

Since 2016, Threema AG publishes a [[transparency report]] where public authority inquiries are disclosed.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |url=https://threema.ch/en/transparencyreport |title=Transparency Report |website=threema.ch}}</ref>

On March 9, 2017, Threema was listed in the "Register of organizers of information dissemination in the Internet" operated by the [[Federal Service for Supervision of Communications, Information Technology and Mass Media]] of the Russian Federation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://reestr.rublacklist.net/distributor/108945 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170620101456/https://reestr.rublacklist.net/distributor/108945 |archive-date=20 June 2017 |title=Threema GmbH|work={{ill|rublacklist.net|ru|РосКомСвобода}}|language=ru|access-date=September 20, 2017}}</ref>

In a response, a Threema spokesperson publicly stated:<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ewdn.com/2017/03/16/russia-adds-intrernational-messenger-threema-to-official-registry-with-a-view-to-control-users-communications/|title=Russia adds international messenger Threema to official registry|date=March 16, 2017|website=East-West Digital News|access-date=January 27, 2018}}</ref> <blockquote>"We operate under Swiss law and are neither allowed nor willing to provide any information about our users to foreign authorities."</blockquote>On April 29, 2021, Threema won a significant case at the [[Federal Supreme Court of Switzerland]] against the [[Law enforcement in Switzerland|Swiss Federal Department of Police and Justice]], who wished to classify the company as a telecommunications provider. Had they lost the case, Threema would have had a legal requirement to identify users and send information about their users to law enforcement.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Bannister|first=Adam|date=28 May 2021|title=Threema, the European rival to Signal, wins pivotal privacy battle in Swiss Court|work=The Daily Swig|url=https://portswigger.net/daily-swig/threema-the-european-rival-to-signal-wins-pivotal-privacy-battle-in-swiss-court|access-date=10 Aug 2021}}</ref>

Starting January 2022, [[Swiss Armed Forces]] suggested that the troops should use Threema instead of WhatsApp, Telegram and [[Signal (messaging app)|Signal]], citing Threema being Swiss-based without servers in the [[United States]] and thus not subject to the [[CLOUD Act]], also promising that soldiers would be reimbursed for the cost.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-05|title=Swiss army backs home-grown IM service amid privacy concerns|url=https://apnews.com/article/technology-business-europe-army-instant-messaging-d3c7c8fd54a78e8cc17fe930014d92d2|access-date=2022-01-10|website=AP NEWS|language=en}}</ref>

== Reception ==
In February 2014, German consumer organisation [[Stiftung Warentest]] evaluated several [[Information privacy|data-protection]] aspects of Threema, [[WhatsApp]], [[Telegram (software)|Telegram]], [[BlackBerry Messenger]] and [[Line (software)|Line]]. 

It considered the security of the data transmission between clients, the services' [[Terms of service|terms of use]], the transparency of the service providers, the availability of the source code, and the apps' overall availability. 

Threema was the only app rated as 'non-critical' (''{{Lang|de|unkritisch}}'') in relation to data and privacy protection, but lost marks due to its closed-source nature, though this has changed for its frontend clients since the end of 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.test.de/WhatsApp-und-Alternativen-Datenschutz-im-Test-4675013-0/ |title=WhatsApp und Alternativen: Datenschutz im Test |date=February 26, 2014 |website=[[Stiftung Warentest]] |language=de |trans-title=WhatsApp and alternatives: data protection tested |access-date=October 30, 2020}}</ref>

Along with [[Cryptocat]] and [[Surespot]], Threema was ranked first in a study evaluating the security and usability of instant messaging encryption software, conducted by the German PSW Group in June 2014.<ref>{{cite web |first=Christian |last=Heutger |url=http://www.psw-group.de/blog/die-ergebnisse-unseres-grossen-messenger-tests/1297#more-1297 |title=Die Ergebnisse unseres großen Messenger-Tests |trans-title=The results of our great messenger test |date=June 13, 2014 |website=PSW Group |access-date=October 30, 2020 |language=de}}</ref>

{{As of|2015|11}}, Threema had a score of 6 out of 7 points on the – now withdrawn and outdated – [[Electronic Frontier Foundation]]'s "Secure Messaging Scorecard". It received points for having communications encrypted in transit, having communications encrypted with keys the provider doesn't have access to (i.e. having [[end-to-end encryption]]), making it possible for users to independently verify their correspondent's identities, having past communications secure if the keys are stolen (i.e. implementing [[forward secrecy]]), having its security design well-documented and having completed an independent security audit.

It lost a point because its source code was not open to independent review (i.e. it was not [[open-source software|open-source]], though in late 2020 its client apps were open-sourced, leaving only its server daemons proprietary).<ref>{{cite web|date=November 3, 2015|title=Secure Messaging Scorecard. Which apps and tools actually keep your messages safe?|url=https://www.eff.org/secure-messaging-scorecard|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160414190543/https://www.eff.org/secure-messaging-scorecard|archive-date=April 14, 2016|access-date=October 30, 2020|website=Electronic Frontier Foundation}}</ref>

Since May 2023, Threema and several other encrypted messaging apps are banned in India for their alleged use by [[Terrorism in India|terrorists]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-01 |title=India has blocked 14 mobile messenger apps on security fears |url=https://qz.com/india-has-blocked-14-messenger-apps-on-security-fears-1850390425 |access-date=2025-04-28 |website=Quartz |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=India first democracy to ban encrypted messaging apps on massive scale. |url=https://tuta.com/blog/apps-banned-india |access-date=2025-04-28 |website=Tuta |language=en-US}}</ref>
